I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou best. I farm in the North China Plain, so I want a steady, familiar system that matches my labor, water, and the weather. I will sow winter wheat on all my main field land first, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same land. I choose improved wheat seed because it is stable and easier for me to manage, and I choose hybrid maize because maize hybrids usually yield better and stand stronger. I will use moderate fertilizer rather than pushing too hard, because I want dependable output and I do not want to waste money. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, one or two topdressings, and several irrigations at key stages. For maize, I will fertilize at planting and again around jointing, and I will irrigate only when needed because summer rain helps. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and common for my kind of field work, and I will spray pesticides only as needed for the usual local pests and diseases. This is the plan I would follow because it is the most reliable way for me to protect yield and reduce risk over the full year.
